_comment.1: STANDALONE parport_dac 2V test -- no camera, no FSM. Drives a constant
_comment.2: 2.0 V onto DACA (channel 0) of the BP-DAC81404EVM and holds it there so
_comment.3: you can confirm it on a meter. Uses the "+-10" bipolar range to match
_comment.4: the bench's actual jumpering/supplies (J11 to 1-2, AVSS = -15 V on J17
_comment.5: pin 5, AVDD = +15 V on J17 pin 4, DVDD = 5 V on J17 pin 1 -- 3.3 V is NOT
_comment.6: enough for DVDD), same as the sine smoke test, not the unipolar default.
_comment.8: The 2.0 V comes entirely from parport_dac's own "offset" param, with
_comment.9: "scale" set to 0 -- so the pipeline's command value is multiplied away
_comment.10: and the output is exactly offset, every iteration, regardless of what
_comment.11: test_source sends. That decouples the voltage from any upstream noise
_comment.12: or clipping, which is what you want for a fixed reference-voltage check.
_comment.14: "verify": true reads each write back over SDO/ACK (DB25 pin 10, which
_comment.15: is wired on this bench) and warns if the DAC doesn't confirm 2.0 V.
_comment.16: IMPORTANT CAVEAT (2026-07-28, after reading a local copy of the DAC81404
_comment.17: datasheet, dac81404.pdf): the frame/readback format itself is now
_comment.18: confirmed from the datasheet text, and parport_dac.c now forces
_comment.19: SPICONFIG.FSDO=1 so SDO updates on the edges this code samples. What is
_comment.20: still NOT confirmed is which AX99100 status-register bit ACK physically
_comment.21: lands on for THIS card (not in the DAC datasheet at all -- only the
_comment.22: data/control pin levels were bench-measured) and whether the DAC
_comment.23: preloads its first readback bit before any clock edge. Watch the log
_comment.24: for 'readback echo mismatch' -- if you see it, ack_status_bit (default
_comment.25: 6) or that alignment assumption is wrong, and a quiet run should not be
_comment.26: trusted as proof until that's resolved.
_comment.28: ALSO NOTE: parport_dac.c previously never cleared SPICONFIG.DEV-PWDWN,
_comment.29: a device-wide power-down bit that defaults to 1 at reset -- separate
_comment.30: from GENCONFIG's reference power-down and DACPWDWN's per-channel bits,
_comment.31: both of which WERE already being cleared. That means every prior bench
_comment.32: session that only measured SPI bus timing (frames/s) rather than an
_comment.33: actual output voltage could have been talking to a device that was
_comment.34: still device-wide powered down the whole time. This is now fixed (init
_comment.35: writes SPICONFIG before GENCONFIG), so this file is a genuine first
_comment.36: test of whether the DAC actually outputs anything at all, not just of
_comment.37: whether the bus wiring is right.
_comment.39: MUST RUN AS ROOT (mapping a PCI BAR needs CAP_SYS_RAWIO), and it unbinds
_comment.43: Wiring (matches what's already on the bench): DB25 pin 2 = D0 = SCLK,
_comment.44: pin 3 = D1 = SDIN, pin 4 = D2 = SYNC, pin 10 = ACK = SDO (readback),
_comment.45: grounds 18-25 -> EVM J4 pin 2 AND J1 pin 4 (both -- SCLK is on J1,
_comment.46: SDIN/SYNC on J4). LDAC tied low via a grounded wire (same effect as
_comment.47: the EVM's own J2 1-2 jumper). Pin names here are the DAC81404's own
_comment.48: (SYNC/LDAC, no "Z" -- confirmed against the datasheet); the EVM's own
_comment.49: schematic net label for the SYNC net happens to be DAC_SYNCZ, which is
_comment.50: the board's notation, not the chip's pin name.
_comment.52: There is no stop_after_count -- it holds 2 V forever until Ctrl+C. On
_comment.53: exit, parport_dac_fini() only idles the SPI bus (SCLK/SYNC high); it
_comment.54: does NOT write a new code to the DAC, so the DAC81404's internal DAC0
_comment.55: register keeps holding the 2 V code and the output stays at 2 V after
_comment.56: the process exits, until something else writes that register or resets
_comment.59: To check the plumbing without root, set backend to "ppdev" (slow, ~4 us
_comment.60: per edge -- fine for a static level like this).

params._range: 0-5, matching the steering/bode par configs; 76 uV/LSB instead of the +-10 range's 305 uV, which matters for a DC park-and-measure check. `offset` is the voltage under test and is left at 3.0 V rather than moved to the 2.5 V bias -- it is this file's whole parameter. Anything in 0..5 V is valid.
